metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bayfield, CO
metaDescription: Bayfield sits in La Plata County's San Juan Basin, one of the earliest major coalbed methane plays. See how legacy Fruitland Formation production affects your minerals.
heroLead: Bayfield sits in La Plata County within the San Juan Basin, one of the earliest and largest coalbed methane plays in the country, where Fruitland Formation gas production dates back to the 1990s and, in places, even earlier conventional gas history before that.
intro: This basin's CBM development predates the Raton Basin's boom by a decade or more, and many wells here have been producing steadily for twenty-five years or longer. If your family holds minerals connected to a Bayfield-area legal description, the interest may be tied to some of the longest-running continuous production in the state, which tends to make ownership history and decimal interest confirmation more important than guessing at future development potential.

sections.heading: A mature basin with a long production tail
paragraphs: Fruitland Formation coalbed methane wells in this area have generally moved well past their peak dewatering-driven production and into a long, low-decline tail. That's actually a favorable characteristic for valuing a producing interest, since the production trend is well established and predictable rather than the kind of steep early decline you'd see on a newer horizontal oil well elsewhere in the state.

sections.heading: La Plata County records and long ownership chains
paragraphs: Because production here has run for decades, it's common for a mineral interest to have passed through two or three generations of the same family since the original lease was signed. The La Plata County Clerk and Recorder in Durango holds that full deed and probate chain, and confirming your current decimal share against it is the necessary first step before any offer.

sections.heading: What we check before quoting
paragraphs: We build a decline curve from actual multi-year royalty history where available, since this basin's long production record gives us more data to work with than a newer play would. For non-producing or unleased tracts, we weigh the basin's mature, largely built-out development stage realistically.

faqs.question: How long has production been running near Bayfield?
faqs.answer: Some San Juan Basin CBM wells have been producing continuously since the 1990s, among the longest-running coalbed methane production in the country.

faqs.question: Does a long production history make my interest easier to value?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since decades of production data give a clear, well-established decline trend to work from rather than an estimate.

faqs.question: My family's lease has changed hands multiple times over the decades — can you still confirm ownership?
faqs.answer: Yes, we trace the full deed and assignment chain through La Plata County records to confirm your current interest.

faqs.question: Is there still new drilling in this part of the basin?
faqs.answer: The San Juan Basin is a mature play with limited new drilling compared to its 1990s peak. We check current activity against your specific tract rather than assuming a flat answer.
